title: Procedures — Engine Start and Cold Weather Start Technique
abstract: Flight crew procedure for engine start, including the automatic start sequence, the crew monitoring points and the technique and expectations when starting after a cold soak.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the flight crew procedure for starting the engines, the parameters to monitor during the sequence and the additional considerations that apply after a cold soak.
sections.description: Engine start is automatic. The aeroplane opens the start valve, motors the engine, introduces fuel and ignition at the correct point and monitors the sequence to completion, aborting it and annunciating if a parameter is exceeded. The crew monitors the sequence rather than controlling it. After a cold soak the engine will light later and peak at a higher exhaust gas temperature than in temperate conditions, and the two engines may differ noticeably from each other in both respects. A difference between the engines during a cold start is not by itself an abnormality provided no parameter is exceeded and both starts complete; it should be recorded in the technical log so that maintenance can trend it. Bleed air for the start comes from the auxiliary power unit or from a ground source, and a low supply pressure lengthens the motoring phase.
sections.crew_procedure: Select the engine start selector to start and the master switch on for the selected engine. Monitor the motoring speed, the exhaust gas temperature and the fuel flow at the points given in the procedure. If a parameter approaches its limit, be prepared for the automatic abort and do not intervene unless the aeroplane fails to abort. After a cold soak start, note the peak exhaust gas temperature for each engine and record any difference greater than sixty degrees in the technical log. Do not attempt a second start on an engine that has aborted until the published cooling period has passed.
sections.limitation_note: The starter duty cycle and the maximum start exhaust gas temperature are in the limitations section. A start that exceeds the temperature limit requires an engineering inspection before the next flight.

type_data.crew_action: Monitor the automatic start sequence; record any start temperature difference greater than 60 degrees.

Configuration note: this entry was reviewed against the air starter heat shield and duct standoff change of MOD-168252 and is unaffected by it. The change is confined to the shield, its standoffs and the harness retention behind them; it alters neither the start sequence, nor the motoring or light-up behaviour, nor any parameter the crew monitors, and it introduces no new crew action and no limitation. The review is recorded here so that the same assessment is not repeated the next time the starter installation is touched.
